title: From Event to Formation
headline: Facts vs. Stories: How Events Shape You
tagline: The event happened once. Your interpretation may replay it a thousand times.
seo_title: Facts vs. Stories: How One Event Shapes Who You Become | TheWrkShop
seo_description: What happened matters, but so does what happens inside you afterward. A devotional for men on separating the event from the story you tell about it.
verse_text: ….we take captive every thought to make it obedient to Christ.

scriptures.text: ….we take captive every thought to make it obedient to Christ.
Everyone should be quick to listen, slow to speak and slow to become angry….

items: Something happened.
They said it.
You were overlooked.
You received criticism.
Someone offended you.
That is the event.

blocks.text: But something can happen once externally and continue happening internally for hours, days, months or even years.
The event happened once. Your interpretation may replay it a thousand times.
Every replay can become another opportunity for anger, fear, shame, bitterness, comparison…. or truth.

items: Someone doesn’t invite you. Fact: you weren’t invited.
Your boss corrects your work. Fact: you received correction.
Someone else succeeds. Fact: they succeeded.
Faithful interpretation is not optimistic editing.
If someone betrayed you, the betrayal matters.
If you failed, the failure matters.
Joseph did not deny the evil done to him. He said, “You intended to harm me….”
Then he expanded the frame: “….but God intended it for good.”
He named the harm without allowing the harm to become the whole story.

sections.label: 2. The Interpretation: What Did You Decide It Meant?

items: Someone doesn’t invite you. Story: “They don’t like me.”
Your boss corrects your work. Story: “They don’t respect me.”
Someone else succeeds. Story: “I’m falling behind.”
Fact. Story.
The story may be correct.
But it must be tested.
Your first interpretation does not always deserve the final word.
Fear speaks quickly.
Shame speaks quickly.
Anger speaks quickly.
One painful moment should not be allowed to write a theology about everything.
A thought can enter without receiving permission to govern.
What happened does not automatically have the right to decide who you become.
Same event. Different agreement. Different direction.
